hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive muscle weakness, fatigue, and palpitations. ECG shows peaked T waves, loss of P waves, widened QRS. Labs reveal severe hyperkalemia (K+ >6.5). Medication history: on ACE inhibitor for HTN and recently started NSAIDs for joint pain. ACEI reduces aldosterone → decreased renal K+ excretion. NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow → further decrease K+ excretion. Combined → dangerous hyperkalemia. Management: IMMEDIATE cardiac membrane stabilization — IV calcium gluconate or calcium chloride (does NOT lower K+, PROTECTS the heart). Then shift K+ intracellularly: IV regular insulin + glucose, beta-agonist (albuterol nebulized), sodium bicarbonate if acidotic. Then eliminate K+: furosemide (if renal function adequate), sodium polystyrene sulfonate (Kayexalate), patiromer, or hemodialysis if refractory. Discontinue ACEI and NSAIDs.
